## Orca worktree rules

Applies to agents in an Orca task worktree (`cc-*` Claude, `cx-*` Codex). The
master session follows the `orca-dev-ops` skill instead.

- The master session plans, reviews, commits, rebases, merges, and pushes.
  Implement the plan it sent without re-planning, and ask through
  `orca orchestration ask` when the plan is unclear.
- When a step does not need the master's input, keep going. Stop and ask
  through `orca orchestration ask` only when you cannot continue without the
  master, or before anything destructive.
- Destructive means: deleting files outside this worktree, `git reset --hard`
  or `git clean -fd`, large dependency changes, and database or
  external-service operations. Permission prompts are off in this workflow;
  the PreToolUse guard (Claude) and the sandbox (Codex) block known
  destructive operations. For anything else destructive, ask the master first.
- The master starts every child as a dispatched worker. Ask through
  `orca orchestration ask`; it blocks until the master replies. Only if the
  command fails, write the question or report on screen and stop.
- Leave all changes uncommitted. Never run `git commit`, `push`, `merge`, or
  `rebase`, never touch `master`, and never create or remove worktrees.
- Report exactly once with `orca orchestration send --type worker_done
  --outcome succeeded|failed`, whose body is the five-line report: result /
  changed files / verification (commands run + last lines of output) /
  blocked on master / found. Use `--outcome failed` when blocked; never exit
  silently.
- Never run a command that does not exit on its own (dev servers, watch
  modes, interactive prompts) in the foreground; run it in the background
  with a timeout. Never end a turn waiting on your own background job
  without an open `ask` or a sent `worker_done`.
- For long multi-step tasks, keep `TASKS.md` at the worktree root updated with
  done / in progress / not started / found issues. Never commit it.
- When the master sends a follow-up mid-run, stop the current work at a clean
  point, then apply it.
- Run the verification this repository requires before reporting done.
- Do not edit a file another active task worktree has declared in its scope.
<!-- orca-worktree-rules:end -->
